readiness_note: Check the actual language, motor and learning demands; age does not imply independent reading, writing or conflict management.
title: Ask a specific learning question
description: Practice indicating the exact part of a learning activity that needs explanation or support.

adaptations: Offer speech, pointing, drawing, objects, signing or AAC; allow extra processing time and an adult to do the writing.
avoid: Do not make a child attempt a fixed number of failures before asking.
Do not mistake inaccessible work or missing teaching for low effort.
parent.review_guidance: Notice whether the action is usable and welcome, not how many perfect days occur. Reduce the step or change the environment when it adds strain; discuss persistent difficulty with the relevant educator or professional.
parent.say: You can show me the confusing part; you do not have to struggle alone first.
parent.selection_guidance: Choose this when help is available but the child cannot show what is confusing. First make help emotionally safe and check whether the task requires new teaching or accommodations.
parent.setup: Offer a help card next to the activity and read directions when needed.
steps: Respond to help promptly; help does not have to be earned.
Model a specific question such as “What does this word mean?”
Accept pointing to the confusing part and provide teaching or a school follow-up.

kid.description: Tell someone which bit is tricky.
kid.help_phrase: Can you help me with this?
kid.title: Ask one learning question

practice.completion: Child points to or asks about one part; adult responds.
practice.observation_rule: Record actual participation separately from pass, pause or observation. Do not score feelings, compliance, disclosure or independence. Outgoing events require separate observation.
practice.stretch_version: Ask one question about the example.
practice.timing_note: Editorial estimate of this card's micro-action, not a deadline or the full activity/care/recovery duration.

not_for: Not for requiring failed attempts, precise speech, a diagnosis or a polished question before help. Not a substitute for missing teaching or needed accommodations.

evidence.age_transfer: Correlational school/college samples; K–8 overlap, not preschool causal evidence.
evidence.does_not_establish: The exact micro-habit, app card and stacking sequence were not tested.
evidence.supports: Autonomy-supportive parenting is associated with adaptive functioning, with confounding limitations.

evidence.age_transfer: Developmental review across childhood/adulthood, not age-specific microhabit trials.
evidence.does_not_establish: The exact micro-habit, app card and stacking sequence were not tested.
evidence.supports: Development and context constrain task performance, supporting adult scaffolding.

research.insight: Autonomy-support and developmental guidance favor responsive scaffolding. Specific help-question practice is a proposed support behavior; no cited trial isolates this card.
